subject: math
title: Change in Quantity to 20: Some Come, Some Go
seo_title: Grade 1 Math Change in Quantity to 20 Worksheets: Free, with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Change in quantity to 20, concretely and verbally
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 math worksheets on change in quantity to 20, following the BC curriculum: some more come, some go away, what changed, and same or changed, with pictures and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Some more come: the number goes up. Some go away: it goes down.
key_sub: 8 salmon and 4 more swim in: 8 + 4 = 12. 13 kids and 5 go to the swings: 13 − 5 = 8. Before 8, now 12? 4 came.
body_html:
The idea: a number can change

Start with a group. Then something happens. Some more come: the number goes up. Some go away: the number goes down. If nothing comes or goes, it stays the same.

Say it in words: “I had 8. 4 more came. Now I have 12.”

What happensThe numberExample
Some more comegoes up8 + 4 = 12
Some go awaygoes down13 − 5 = 8
Some come, the same number gostays the same6 + 2 − 2 = 6

Some more come

Show the first group. Show the ones that come. Count them all.

Some go away

Show them all. Cross out the ones that go away. Count the ones that are left.

What changed?

Put the “before” group over the “now” group. Match them one to one. The extra ones show the change.

How many went away?

There were 15 eagles in a cedar tree. Some flew away. Now there are 9. How many flew away?

There are fewer now, so some went away. Count up from 9 to 15: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. That is 6.

Answer: 6 eagles

Same or changed?

Sometimes some come and then the same number go away. Then there is no change.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding when some went away: 13 − 5 is not 18Some went away, so there are fewer. Subtract: 13 − 5 = 8.
Giving the start number: “8” for 8 + 4The number changed. Count the new group: 12.
Giving the “now” number when asked how many cameCount on from the start to the now number: 8 to 12 is 4.
Mixing up more and fewerIs the new group bigger or smaller? Bigger means some came.

faq.q: What does “change in quantity to 20” mean in BC Grade 1 math?
faq.a: It means seeing how a group of up to 20 things changes when some come or some go away. Children show the change with objects and say it in words, like “I had 8, 4 more came, now I have 12.”

faq.q: Why is change in quantity part of patterning in the BC curriculum?
faq.a: It is an early step toward algebra. Children look at a start number, a change and a new number, and learn that adding makes a group bigger and taking away makes it smaller.

faq.q: How can I help my child with “how many came?” questions?
faq.a: Start at the first number and count on to the new number, holding up a finger for each count. From 8 to 12 is 9, 10, 11, 12, so 4 came.

faq.q: How can my child practise change in quantity at home?
faq.a: Use real things like crackers, toys or coins. Put out a group, add or take away a few, and ask “Are there more or fewer now? How many changed?”
